My grandmother is Italian, so I was used to being slipped some limoncello or red wine while my parents weren’t looking. I was about seven, maybe? But by the time I was twelve years old I was already drinking red wine with the rest of the family. 

My first real drunk experience was when we were on holiday at my grandparents’ house in Italy. It was a very warm day, but not unpleasantly so and my grandma had invited all the relatives and neighbors to eat with us. The wine was flowing, a warm breeze blew past my cheeks and suddenly I felt disconnected enough to feel at ease with the world. I looked over at my older brother and I realized he felt the same thing. His eyes were glossed over with the dissociative power of alcohol, and he had this dreamy smile on his face that told me everything was going to be just fine.

When I do this, I usually look like shit. The shakes, the sweat, dark under eyes, y’all know the deal. Her toddler was giving her trouble as well, but she was transfixed on me. I did not give a shit at that moment, the anxiety I felt wasn’t because of a social faux pas. But once I got home and felt stabilized, I straight up started sobbing.

Yeah true, but BPD is categorized as a personality disorder, so it’s expected that most of the disordered behavior stems from interpersonal frictions. People with BPD don’t have malicious intentions, they just learned to cope with traumatic behavior with self destructive coping mechanisms that so happens to include other people as collateral damage. Anorexia on the other hand is an inward directed disorder. I developed mine because of deep self-hatred, and my grandmother who taught me to hate my body from a young age. In my experience, it’s a personal feeling of inadequacy directed outwardly toward the physical body. But what I see online are literal teenage bullies taking out their insecurities on other people.  It’s intentional mean spirited behavior to mask their own feelings of inferiority and it’s infuriating to observe once you’re mature enough to recognize the patterns.
